title: U.S. House · California's 34th District
area: Parts of central and eastern Los Angeles, including Downtown LA, Boyle Heights, East LA, Highland Park, Koreatown, Chinatown, and Eagle Rock.

context.text: California uses a top-two nonpartisan primary. In the June 2, 2026 primary, incumbent Jimmy Gomez (D) placed first with 46.0% and Angela Gonzales-Torres (D) placed second with 30.7%, so both Democrats advance to the November general election; no Republican advanced.

summary.text: Jimmy Gomez is the incumbent U.S. Representative for California's 34th District, serving on the House Committee on Ways and Means and the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence.

background.text: Earned a B.A. in political science from the University of California, Los Angeles, and a master's degree in public policy from Harvard University's John F. Kennedy School of Government.
Served as political director for the United Nurses Associations of California before being elected to Congress.

priorities.text: In his most recent completed Ballotpedia survey (2020), described himself as a 'working-class progressive' and cited co-sponsoring the Green New Deal, Medicare for All, the Rent Relief Act, the George Floyd Justice in Policing Act, and the American Dream and Promise Act.
priorities.quote: I am a co-sponsor of the Green New Deal, Medicare for All, the Rent Relief Act, the George Floyd Justice in Policing Act, and the American Dream and Promise Act.

positions.summary: Co-sponsored Medicare for All, according to his 2020 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response.
positions.quote: I am a co-sponsor of the Green New Deal, Medicare for All, the Rent Relief Act, the George Floyd Justice in Policing Act, and the American Dream and Promise Act.

positions.summary: Co-sponsored the Green New Deal, according to his 2020 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response.
positions.quote: I am a co-sponsor of the Green New Deal, Medicare for All, the Rent Relief Act, the George Floyd Justice in Policing Act, and the American Dream and Promise Act.

positions.summary: Co-sponsored the Rent Relief Act, according to his 2020 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response.
positions.quote: I am a co-sponsor of the Green New Deal, Medicare for All, the Rent Relief Act, the George Floyd Justice in Policing Act, and the American Dream and Promise Act.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Ways and Means (Tax and Work and Welfare subcommittees) and the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence in the 119th Congress (2025–2026).

summary.text: Angela Gonzales-Torres is a community organizer and equity and justice advocate running as a Democrat against incumbent Jimmy Gomez, after placing second in the June 2026 top-two primary.

background.text: Describes herself as a lifelong Angeleno and 'the daughter of a deportee' whose path went from community organizer to congressional candidate.
background.quote: Angela Gonzales-Torres is a lifelong Angeleno, the daughter of a deportee, and an equity and justice advocate.

background.text: Placed second in the June 2, 2026 nonpartisan primary with 30.7% of the vote (36,708 votes), advancing to a same-party general election against incumbent Jimmy Gomez.

priorities.text: Campaign lists four priorities: 'Affordability' (fighting for working people), 'Accountability' (equitably taxing and investing), 'Access' (funding education and youth programs), and 'Abolition' (ending ICE and for-profit prisons).

positions.summary: Campaign site says she is co-sponsoring Medicare for All and investing in mental health, addiction care, and local clinics for everyone regardless of immigration status or income.
positions.quote: Angela is fighting to make that a reality by co-sponsoring Medicare for All, investing in mental health and addiction care, and strengthening local clinics that serve everyone, regardless of immigration status or income.

positions.summary: Campaign site says she is fighting for a 'community-driven Green New Deal' prioritizing renewable energy and unionized green jobs.
positions.quote: Angela is fighting for a bold, community-driven Green New Deal that prioritizes renewable energy, unionized green jobs, and neighborhood-level projects like rooftop gardens, urban farms, and native plant healing spaces.

positions.summary: Campaign site says she supports expanding emergency rental assistance and housing vouchers and building permanently affordable housing.
positions.quote: I'm fighting for bold, people-first housing policies — from expanding emergency rental assistance and housing vouchers to supporting community land trusts and rapid rehousing programs.

positions.summary: Campaign lists 'Abolition' — ending ICE and for-profit prisons — as one of her four core priorities, and calls for a pathway to citizenship and expanded services for mixed-status households.

researchNotes: Gomez has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey and no current issues page was found on his campaign materials, so his 2026 priorities/positions rely on his last completed (2020) survey, cited as dated context. Gonzales-Torres has not completed a Candidate Connection survey; her positions come from her campaign website. Federal key votes and FEC finance totals for both candidates are added separately by script.
